title: Robotic Mirror Therapy System for Functional Recovery of Hemiplegic Arms
protocol: Obtain 3 commercially available AHRS sensors.
Connect the AHRS sensor to a PC with a USB connector.
Use hyperterminal or other communication software to configure general sensor settings.
Set AHRS sensor to RS232 communication mode.
Select appropriate COM port for the sensor.
Set baud rate to 115,200 bits per second.
Set data bits to 8.
Set parity to none.
Set stop bits to 1.
Set flow control to none.
Click home button on bottom left corner of interface.
Right click on computer and click Properties.
Click Device Manager in the properties window.
Expand Port (COM & LPT) tab by clicking it.
Check COM port settings for established communication.
Set channel to 100 for each sensor.
Assign unique IDs to each sensor.
Calibrate accelerometer, gyroscope, and magnetometer if necessary.
Set output format as quaternions.
Configure sensors to display battery reserve information.
Prepare two high-performance brushless DC motors and controllers.
Connect power cable of each controller to a power supply.
Connect motor cable to the motor for each controller.
Connect Hall sensor cable to the motor for each controller.
Connect encoder cable to the motor for each controller.
Connect CAN-CAN cable between controllers.
Set node ID for each controller to distinguish them.
Connect USB cable from PC to each controller for configuration.
Switch on power supply to activate controllers and motors.
Use system configuration software provided by motor manufacturer.
Configure angle limits for safe operation.
Configure home position in the system configuration software.
Put one of the coupling bodies with keyway on the elbow joint motor shaft.
Secure the coupling body using an M5 hex socket set screw.
Attach "Elbow coupling hollow cylinder cover" to the elbow motor using 4x M5 socket head screws (10 mm).
Place the buffer part of the couplings on top of the coupling body attached in step 2.3.1.
Plug the ball bearing into "Elbow rooftop frame".
Secure the ball bearing with 4x M4 socket head screws (8 mm).
Plug "Elbow motor force dispersion shaft" into "Lower elbow support".
Secure it with 4x M3 socket head screws (6 mm).
Place "Upper elbow support" on top of the "Lower elbow support".
Secure "Upper elbow support" using 8x M3 socket head screws (12 mm).
Assemble the part from step 2.3.4 on top.
Insert the assembly from step 2.3.3 in the middle.
Place the last coupling body at the bottom.
Join all parts together and secure the coupling body with M5 hex socket set screws (10 mm).
Secure assembly from step 2.3.5 and assembly from step 2.3.2 using 4x M5 socket head screws (15 mm).
Rotate assembly in step 2.3.2 to secure all four points.
Secure "Lower wrist coupling hollow cylinder cover" with the wrist motor using 4x M4 socket head screws.
Place one of the coupling bodies with keyway on the motor shaft and secure it using M4 hex socket set screws.
Attach the buffer part of the couplings on top of the coupling body.
Attach "Friction reduction ring" on top of "Wrist rooftop frame" with double-sided tape or adhesive.
Plug "Wrist motor force dispersion shaft" into "Handle" and secure it using 4x M2.5 socket head screws.
Place assembly in step 2.3.9 on top, assembly in step 2.3.8 in the middle, and the last part of the coupling body at the bottom.
Join all parts together and secure the coupling body with M4 hex socket set screws.
Secure "Wrist motor2roof2" with the assembly from step 2.3.10 using 4x M3 socket head screws.
Secure assembly in step 2.3.11 and assembly in step 2.3.7 using 4x M3 socket head screws.
Secure 2 "Joint movement limiter" and 2 shaft collars using 4x M4 socket head screws.
Use shaft collars to secure shafts and "Wrist rooftop frame" using 8x M3 socket head screws.
Slide shaft collars in assembly 2.3.13 into the shafts in assembly 2.3.14.
Secure additional shaft collars with "Lower elbow support" using 4x M4 socket head screws.
Join the two parts and secure with a lever.
Secure "Support wall" to the assembly in step 2.3.15 using 6x M4 socket head screws (15 mm).
Secure the table stand and assembly in step 2.3.16 using 6x M6 socket head screws (15 mm).
Establish communication with motors and sensors.
Initialize values for motors and sensors.
Move motors and sensors to initial position.
Enter main loop of program.
Read current position values from Attitude and Heading Reference System (AHRS) sensors.
Transform quaternion data into desired angles for robot motion.
Choose a sensor coordinate frame as reference.
Reset other sensor coordinate frames based on the chosen reference.
Use inverse kinematics to obtain final output yaw angles.
Check motors' positions using motor encoders.
Update motor values to achieve movement to desired position.
Record all angles and angular velocities from AHRS sensors.
Exit the loop once tasks are completed and the stop button is pressed.
Move the robot to its initial position.
Add "error in" functions to detect errors during execution.
Add "error out" functions to debug errors during execution.
Add a patient-side button to choose the robot operation side (patient's paretic side).
Construct a patient information box to identify patients.
Add motor status indicators for monitoring.
Add angle limitation controls for safety purposes.
Configure maximum velocity, acceleration, and deceleration settings for each motor to prevent injuries due to stiff upper limb movement.
Retrieve motor position and velocity information using indicators.
Input current information as needed.
Build a VISA resource name control to establish communication between AHRS sensors and the system.
Add a calibration function to eliminate accumulated sensor drift errors.
Arrange indicator displays to retrieve joint angles and battery reserve from sensors.
Select motors with sufficient torque output for each joint to overcome spasticity.
Ensure wrist motor can exert at least 10 Nm of torque.
Ensure elbow motor can exert at least 25 Nm of torque.
Use straps made of semi-elastic material to fix the forearm in the robot exoskeleton.
Use 2 solid frames combined with a shaft collar to isolate and fix wrist motion.
Fix the hand to the robot using straps around the handle.
Adjust height and width of the task table according to the patient's condition.
Place a mirror in the midline between both arms on a table or platform.
Place AHRS sensors on the handle, wrist frame, and edge of the platform on the healthy side.
Align the sensor's internal yaw axis pointing up parallel with the robot's orientation.
Execute the therapy software on a computer.
Choose the hemiplegic side by clicking the Patient-Side switch button.
Set the maximum joint angle limits according to patient's joint condition.
Use elbow flexion limit less than 50º and elbow extension limit more than -70º for safe operation.
Use wrist flexion limit less than 80º and wrist extension limit more than -60º for safe operation.
Set maximum velocity between 0 and 22.5 rpm for elbow motor.
Set maximum velocity between 0 and 33 rpm for wrist motor.
Fill out patient information.
Turn on all AHRS Sensors before running the program.
Run the program by clicking the arrow button in the upper left corner of the program.
Write proper file names for result data when "save as" prompt pops up.
Press calibration button to initialize sensor values to zero at initial position.
Press STOP button when all tasks are completed.
Conduct a clinical study on healthy subjects to confirm safety and feasibility.
Give the instruction "Do not move your hemiplegic arm on your own" to the subjects for completely passive movement of hemiplegic arm.
Place both forearms on the frames, and hands on the handles.
Fix the forearms with straps.

Conduct functional evaluations such as Fugl-Meyer assessment scale, modified Ashworth scale, modified Barthel index, Jebsen hand function test, hand power measurement, hemispatial neglect test, and motor evoked potential test for the patients before therapy.
Conduct clinical trial for stroke patients with 2-dimensional mirror robot for 30 - 60 min per day.
Give the instruction "Do not move your hemiplegic arm on your own" to the patients during the trial.
After the last session, conduct follow-up functional evaluations.
